text: A substrate was declared procedure-invalid by the operator before any run or reading, with no pre-run rule fired and no written reason recorded, and its nine registered tests stand at a p-value of one with no other label, so the filter is tested on one substrate, a two-dimensional mixture with simulated validators.
citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering (2026). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=7598518

isBasedOn.name: Can Reputation Prevent Model Collapse? A Preregistered Test of Reputation-Weighted Data Filtering

abstract: Intelligence models increasingly learn from data that earlier Intelligence models produced, and when that loop repeats the rare cases disappear first. This paper preregisters a test of whether a reputation-weighted validator pool, filtering the training data of a recursive replacement loop, keeps those rare cases alive. The outcomes remain sealed until a replication of the original model-collapse result succeeds.

additionalProperty.name: scope_conditions
value: The paper draws no inference from the invalidated substrate.
The declaration is one of two departures from the frozen procedure that the paper discloses.

additionalProperty.name: supporting_quote
additionalProperty.value: The operator declared it procedure-invalid before any run or reading. No pre-run rule fired, and no written reason was recorded. Its nine registered tests stand at p equal to 1 with no other label, and the paper draws no inference from it. The consequence is plain: the filter is tested on one substrate, a two-dimensional mixture with simulated validators.
